items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I was one of her good pupils in German.

ctx.x: high school in Jersey, Long Branch. High School, still there, so every day we had a big school orchestra about 20 or 30 pieces, violins and everything, for assembly. We had assembly every morning, at class, and they would play them in and play them out and maybe sometime give a little concert so in the meantime, they had a drummer. The worst thing in the band was the drummer, but he was in a lot of my classes.

I had taken languages too and I was one of the good pupils-a German lady named Madam Bruskey, I was one of her good pupils in German. So anyway he was the dumbest guy, this guy, I said, 'how come you don't have to make up no classes.' He said, 'Oh, I got to rehearse,' and he'd get away with it.

So that went on a long time, so in the meantime I lost my job caddying by this incident. One day we was out and I was caddying for this girl. They didn't have them golf carts then were you could roll them -- you had to carry this heavy bag, and so we were on the course, and halfway to the first, to about the seventh or eighth hole in the rough, this -- she couldn't play no golf but she -- just a sport, because at that time when you see somebody on the golf course, they were very wealthy.
